bug_semantics: Unauthenticated CWE-918 SSRF with HTTP-error reflection in the OIDC token-exchange path. Exchange() takes the Authorization bearer JWT, reads the unverified iss claim via apiauth.ExtractIssuer, and immediately performs OIDC discovery against that string (originally oidc.NewProvider(ctx, issuer); later provider.Get → oidc.NewProvider). go-oidc GETs {iss}/.well-known/openid-configuration and follows redirects using the default HTTP client, so a crafted iss (http://internal-host, link-local metadata, attacker HTTPS that 302s internally) causes the server to fetch attacker-chosen URLs before any signature or trust-policy check. Discovery failures are wrapped into the gRPC error (go-oidc formats '%s: %s' with status and body), so internal response bodies can reflect to the caller; later logging of provider/token-exchange errors added a second leak. Affected <= v0.5.2; first patched v0.5.3.

reasoning: CVE-2025-52477/GHSA-h3qp-hwvr-9xcq is a real published CWE-918, not withdrawn. The attack is unauthenticated: any caller can present a JWT whose payload iss is attacker-controlled; ExtractIssuer does not verify the signature, and OIDC discovery then treats iss as a URL. That mechanism first appears in the initial working tree e6d0bdf230446bcb66f09356053e294659d400ee as the adjacent ExtractIssuer + oidc.NewProvider pair in Exchange(), with discovery errors reflected to the client. The immediate parent e90d1e919d13bb15c45a293c258212651a11777e exists and lacks pkg/octosts entirely, so the vulnerable lines are absent there and no finer public member can be reconstructed. Later 0ba5ef is a cache refactor that relocates NewProvider; 74ba874 bounds response size (different GHSA); 3ae8b79 adds retries on the same sink (v0.5.2). None of those is a first-write of the flawed mechanism. The causal SSRF close is b3976e39bd8c8c217c0670747d34a4499043da92 (issuer/redirect validation), which is not an ancestor of v0.5.2 and is an ancestor of v0.5.3; 0f177fd is defense-in-depth logging redaction on top of that and is the v0.5.3 tag. AI attribution is taken only from the BIC commit object: human author/committer Matt Moore, Signed-off-by only, no AI/bot trailers, so verdict is NOT_AI.
